docs.title: ERB & Shell
docs.text: Prompt files can hold dynamic content. Shell references such as $(git status) are replaced with command output, and ERB tags such as <%= Date.today %> are replaced with the result of Ruby code. Both are on by default.

docs.title: Shell expansion
docs.text:
You write AIA puts in its place $HOME, ${HOME} The environment variable's value, or nothing if it isn't set $(command) The command's standard output, with the trailing newline removed \$ A literal $ 
I am working in $(pwd) on branch $(git branch --show-current).
My editor is $EDITOR.

Here is what changed since yesterday:

$(git log --since=yesterday --oneline)

A few rules keep shell expansion predictable:

  • Only uppercase names are variables. $HOME and $MY_TOKEN are expanded. $price, $5 and $foo are left as they are, so dollar amounts in your text are safe.
  • Fenced code blocks are left alone. Anything between ``` or ~~~ fences reaches the model exactly as written. That way you can show the model a shell example without running it.
  • Command output is not expanded again. If a command prints $HOME or <%= ... %>, that text reaches the model literally. Output can't trigger more expansion or inject Ruby.
  • A failing command stops the run. If a $(...) command exits with a non-zero status, AIA stops and reports the command and its error output. Append || true to a command if failure is acceptable: $(grep TODO *.rb || true).
  • An unmatched $( is an error. Escape a literal one as \$(.

docs.title: ERB
docs.text:
ERB is Ruby's template language. AIA renders every prompt file with ERB after shell expansion.

Tag Meaning <%= expression %> Insert the result of the expression <% code %> Run code without inserting anything (use it for if, each and similar) <%# comment %> A comment that never reaches the model 
Today is <%= Date.today.strftime('%A, %B %-d') %>.

The project has <%= Dir.glob('lib/**/*.rb').size %> Ruby files:
<% Dir.glob('lib/**/*.rb').first(5).each do |f| %>
- <%= f %>
<% end %>

Ruby version: <%= RUBY_VERSION %>

Inside ERB you can use:

  • Parameters: <%= name %>
  • Directives: <%= include 'shared/header.md' %>, <%= webpage 'https://...' %>
  • Plugins: your own helper methods and constants, loaded from the plugins directory
  • Any Ruby code, including backticks: <%= `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.strip %>

docs.title: Shell runs first, then ERB
docs.text:
Shell expansion happens before ERB, so Ruby code can work on shell output:

My OS is <%= "$(uname -s)".downcase %>.
My shell is <%= "$SHELL".split('/').last %>.
  1. Shell expansion produces My OS is <%= "Darwin".downcase %>.
  2. ERB produces My OS is darwin.

Put shell output inside quotes when you use it in Ruby, as shown above.

docs.title: Loading Ruby libraries with --require
docs.text:
ERB can already use the libraries AIA itself loads, such as Date and JSON. To use any other standard library or installed gem in your ERB, load it with --require (short form --rq). Separate several libraries with commas:

<!-- ~/.prompts/sales_summary.md -->
Summarize these sales figures by region:

<% CSV.foreach('sales.csv', headers: true) do |row| %>
- <%= row['region'] %>: <%= row['total'] %>
<% end %>

aia --rq csv sales_summary

To load a library every time, list it in your config file:

# ~/.config/aia/aia.yml
require_libs:
  - json
  - csv

If a library can't be loaded, AIA prints Warning: Failed to require 'name' and keeps going. The first ERB tag that needs the library then fails.

docs.title: Turning processing off for one file
docs.text:
Some prompts contain text that looks like shell or ERB but isn't. Examples are a prompt about writing ERB templates, or one that discusses $(...) syntax. Turn off the stage you don't want in that file's front matter:

---
erb: false     # <%= ... %> is sent literally
shell: false   # $VAR and $(...) are sent literally
---
Explain what this ERB template does:

<%= render partial: 'user', collection: @users %>

Both settings default to true. Each one affects only the file it appears in.

docs.title: Chat input is processed too
docs.text:
Every message you type in a chat session goes through shell expansion and ERB too. You can type:

Follow up (cntl-D or 'exit' to end) #=>
Explain the failures in this output: $(bundle exec rake test 2>&1 | tail -20)

To send a literal $( or <%, escape the dollar sign as \$(, or rephrase. If a message can't be processed, AIA shows the error and doesn't send the message.

docs.title: Running Ruby in chat: /ruby
docs.text:
The /ruby directive (alias /rb) runs a line of Ruby and sends the result to the model:

Follow up (cntl-D or 'exit' to end) #=>
/ruby (1..20).select(&:even?).sum

/ruby is off by default. Turn it on for one session with --allow-ruby-eval:

aia --chat --allow-ruby-eval

or for every session in your config file:

flags:
  allow_ruby_eval: true

While it's off, /ruby only prints an error message. While it's on, AIA prints WARNING: /ruby executing: ... to STDERR before running the code. If the code raises an error, the error message is sent to the model in place of a result.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Prompts are programs

ERB, backticks and $(...) in a prompt file run with your user's permissions as soon as the prompt is rendered. --allow-ruby-eval doesn't control them. It only controls the /ruby chat directive. Read any prompt file you didn't write before you run it, and don't render prompts from untrusted sources. See Security.

docs.title: Executable Prompts
docs.text: An executable prompt is a prompt file that you run like a shell script. Give it a shebang line and make it executable, and ./standup asks the model your question with no aia command to type.

docs.title: Your first executable prompt
docs.text:
Create a file with aia on the shebang line:

cat > fun_fact <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env -S aia --no-output
Tell me one surprising fun fact about a random animal.
Keep it to two sentences.
EOF

chmod +x fun_fact
./fun_fact

When you run ./fun_fact, the system runs aia --no-output ./fun_fact. AIA sees that the file starts with #!, drops that first line, and uses the rest of the file as the prompt.

Anything that works in a regular prompt file also works here. That includes front matter, parameters, shell expansion and ERB:

#!/usr/bin/env -S aia --no-output -t 0.3
---
parameters:
  days: 1
---
Write a short stand-up update from these commits in $(basename $(pwd)):

<%= `git log --since="#{days} days ago" --oneline` %>

Parameters inside commands

Shell expansion runs before ERB, so a $(...) command can't see parameter values. A <%= days %> inside $(...) reaches the shell as literal text. When a command needs a parameter, run it with Ruby backticks inside ERB, as the last line above does.

docs.title: The shebang line
docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env -S aia --no-output
  • -S tells env to split the rest of the line into separate arguments. Linux needs it. macOS splits shebang arguments without it, but -S works on both, so use it.
  • Put AIA options on the shebang line. Any option from the CLI reference can go there, such as --model, --role, --tokens or -c my_config.yml.
  • Use --no-output unless you want a copy of each response in temp.md in whatever directory you run the script from.

A few useful variations:

#!/usr/bin/env -S aia --no-output --model gpt-4o
#!/usr/bin/env -S aia --no-output --role ruby_expert
#!/usr/bin/env -S aia --chat

The last one answers the prompt and then opens a chat session so you can ask follow-up questions.

docs.title: Adding options and files when you run it
docs.text:
Arguments you type after the script name are passed to AIA. Options are applied to that run, and file names become context files added after the prompt:

./fun_fact --model claude-sonnet-4      # use a different model this time
./fun_fact --tokens                     # show token usage
./review_file lib/parser.rb             # add a file for the prompt to work on

Options from the shebang line and options you type are combined. For an option that holds a single value, such as --temperature or --role, the value you type wins. List options such as --model, --next and --pipeline add to what the shebang sets. If the shebang already names a model, typing --model runs both models side by side.

docs.title: Piping input into an executable prompt
docs.text:
Text piped into an executable prompt is added after the prompt:

git diff --cached | ./commit_message

#!/usr/bin/env -S aia --no-output -t 0.2
Write a conventional commit message for the staged diff below.
Subject line under 60 characters, then a short body.

Parameters still work when you pipe input. AIA reads your answers from the terminal, not from the pipe.

docs.title: Prompts without a file
docs.text:
The prompt doesn't have to be in a file at all. When you don't name a prompt ID, whatever arrives on STDIN is the prompt:

echo "Explain the difference between a process and a thread." | aia --no-output

aia --no-output < question.txt

Piped prompts are processed like a prompt file, with front matter, shell expansion and ERB.

If the piped text starts with a #! line, that line is dropped, so you can pipe an executable prompt (cat fun_fact | aia) and its front matter still applies.

docs.title: Where the response goes
docs.text:
The response is printed to standard output. It starts with an AI: label and each line is indented. The progress spinner goes to standard error, so redirecting standard output captures only the response:

./standup > standup.txt
./standup | pbcopy

To save responses to a file with AIA's own output handling, use --output FILE (and --append to keep earlier runs). See Output & History.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• include is not available. An executable prompt isn't in your prompts directory, so <%= include 'file' %> stops with an error. Use <%= insert 'file' %>, which reads the file as-is, relative to your current directory.
  • The prompt runs from your current directory. Relative paths in $(...), ERB and insert are resolved against the directory you run the script from, not the directory that holds the script.

docs.title: Ideas
docs.text:
• Git hooks. A prepare-commit-msg hook that runs git diff --cached | ~/bin/commit_message.
  • Daily reports. A cron job that runs ./standup and mails the result. Give every parameter a default so nothing waits for input.
  • Make targets. review: ; ./prompts/review_changes $(shell git diff --name-only).

Treat executable prompts as scripts

An executable prompt runs shell commands and Ruby code with your permissions. Read one before you run it, just as you would any other script. See Security.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameters turn one prompt file into a template you can use for many inputs. You declare them in the front matter, use them in the body with ERB tags, and AIA asks you for any values it needs when the prompt runs.

docs.title: Declaring parameters
docs.text:
List each parameter under parameters: in the front matter. The value you give it is its default. A parameter with no value (or null) is required.

---
parameters:
  name:              # required: AIA will ask for it
  language: Spanish  # optional: defaults to Spanish
  tone: friendly     # optional: defaults to friendly
---
Write a short greeting for <%= name %> in <%= language %>.
Use a <%= tone %> tone. Keep it to two sentences.

In the body, <%= name %> is replaced by the parameter's value. Parameters use ERB syntax. The [NAME] placeholders from AIA 1.x are not supported. See Migrating Prompts to convert older prompts.

Naming

Use lowercase snake_case names such as file_name or target_audience. A name that starts with a capital letter is read by ERB as a Ruby constant, and the prompt fails to render. Also avoid names of Ruby's built-in methods, such as format, test, select, open or print: <%= format %> calls Ruby's method instead of reading your parameter, and the prompt fails with an ArgumentError.

docs.title: Answering the questions
docs.text:
When the prompt runs, AIA asks for every declared parameter in the order you listed them. The default appears in parentheses:

$ aia --no-output greeting
Value for name (required): Maria
Value for language (Spanish):
Value for tone (friendly): formal
  • Type a value and press Enter to use it.
  • Press Enter on an empty line, or Ctrl+D, to accept the default.
  • For a required parameter, an empty answer stops AIA with Parameter 'name' is required.
  • Ctrl+C cancels with Variable input interrupted.

Each answer is a string. A default in the front matter keeps its YAML type, so count: 3 is the number 3 until you type over it.

AIA reads answers from your terminal even when the prompt's input is piped, so you can mix parameters with piping:

git diff | aia --no-output review_diff
Value for focus (correctness): security

Answers are not remembered

AIA doesn't save your answers between runs. If you find yourself typing the same value every time, make it the default in the front matter.

docs.title: Using parameters in the body
docs.text:
A parameter is just a value inside ERB, so you can do more than print it.

Conditional text:

---
parameters:
  audience: developer
---
<% if audience == "developer" %>
Explain how Ruby's garbage collector works, including generational GC.
<% elsif audience == "manager" %>
Explain what garbage collection is and why it matters for performance.
Keep it non-technical.
<% else %>
Explain garbage collection as if I were ten years old.
<% end %>

Keep your answer to one paragraph.

Transforming the value:

---
parameters:
  topic:
---
Write a blog post titled "<%= topic.split.map(&:capitalize).join(' ') %>".

Reading a file whose name you supply:

---
parameters:
  file_name:
---
Review this file for bugs:

<%= File.read(file_name) %>

docs.title: Parameters and included files
docs.text:
When a prompt pulls in another file with <%= include 'path/to/file.md' %>, the included file sees the same parameter values as the file that includes it. You answer each question once, and both files use the answer.

AIA asks about the parameters declared in the file you run first. A parameter declared only in an included file uses its default from that file. If it has no default, AIA asks for it when the include is reached. See Directives.

docs.title: Parameters in pipelines
docs.text: In a pipeline, AIA asks for each prompt's parameters when that prompt's turn comes. If a pipeline will run unattended, give every parameter a default.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause and fix A tag renders as nothing The name inside <%= %> doesn't match any declared parameter. Unknown names render as an empty string. Check the spelling. parameters must be a mapping parameters: must hold name: value pairs, not a list. You're asked for a value you thought had a default name: with nothing after it means required. Give it a value. The literal text <%= name %> reaches the model The front matter sets erb: false. Remove that line.

docs.title: Pipelines
docs.text: A pipeline runs several prompts one after another in a single conversation. Each prompt can build on the answers to the prompts before it, which lets you split a big job into small, focused steps.

docs.title: How chaining works
docs.text:
All the prompts in a pipeline go to the same conversation. When the second prompt runs, the model has already seen the first prompt and its own answer to it. A later prompt can therefore say "the names above" or "your previous answer" and the model knows what it means.

For example, here are four small prompts:

<!-- brainstorm.md -->
Suggest five names for a Ruby gem that formats log files.

<!-- evaluate.md -->
Rate each of the names above from 1 to 5 for clarity and memorability.

<!-- pick_best.md -->
Pick the single best name from your ratings and explain why in one sentence.

<!-- tagline.md -->
Write a one-line tagline for the gem you picked.

Each one is easy to read and easy to improve on its own. Run together, they produce a researched answer.

docs.title: Defining a pipeline on the command line
docs.text:
The prompt ID you name on the command line runs first. Add more steps with --pipeline or --next.

--pipeline (-p)--next (-n)

Give a comma-separated list of the prompt IDs to run after the first:

aia --pipeline evaluate,pick_best,tagline brainstorm

Add one prompt ID per --next. You can repeat it:

aia brainstorm --next evaluate --next pick_best --next tagline

Both commands run brainstorm, evaluate, pick_best and tagline in that order.

Without a prompt ID, the first prompt in --pipeline runs first: aia -p brainstorm,evaluate,pick_best,tagline runs the same chain.

Before it starts, AIA checks that every prompt ID given on the command line exists. If any is missing, nothing runs:

Error: Prompt ID 'pick_bset' does not exist at /Users/you/.prompts/pick_bset.md
One or more prompt IDs do not exist.

docs.title: Defining a pipeline in front matter
docs.text:
If a set of prompts always runs together, record the chain in the prompt files.

next: names the single prompt to run after this one:

---
next: explain_joke
---
Tell me a short, clean joke about computers.

pipeline: lists every prompt to run after this one:

---
pipeline: [evaluate, pick_best, tagline]
---
Suggest five names for a Ruby gem that formats log files.

Now aia brainstorm runs the whole chain.

Keep these points in mind:

  • pipeline: can be a YAML list or a comma-separated string: pipeline: evaluate, pick_best, tagline.
  • A file can have next: or pipeline:, but not both.
  • next: and pipeline: replace whatever steps were still waiting to run, including steps from --pipeline or --next. Use the command line or front matter for a chain, not both.
  • Any step can set its own next:, so prompts can hand off to each other: a says next: b, b says next: c, and so on.
  • AIA doesn't check prompt IDs from front matter in advance. A misspelled one stops the pipeline when that step is reached.

docs.title: What each step receives
docs.text:
Input Which steps get it The prompt file's own text, after parameters, shell and ERB are processed That step Text piped on STDIN The first step only Context files named on the command line Every step --role Every step (placed in front) --skill Every step (placed after)

Since context files are added to every step, you can give the same source material to a series of different questions:

aia --pipeline find_bugs,suggest_tests summarize_code lib/parser.rb

AIA asks for each step's parameters when that step starts.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: AIA shows each step's response as soon as it arrives, with a separator line between steps. If an output file is set (the default is temp.md), each response is added to it. The file is emptied when the run starts unless you pass --append. Use --no-output to show the responses in the terminal only. See Output & History.

docs.title: Continuing in chat
docs.text:
Add --chat to keep talking once the pipeline finishes. The chat continues the same conversation, so you can ask about any step:

aia --chat --pipeline evaluate,pick_best brainstorm

docs.title: Tracking steps in TrakFlow
docs.text: If you use TrakFlow for task tracking, --track-pipeline records the pipeline as a plan and marks each step as started, completed or failed. See Advanced Modes.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Keep each step to one job. Short, single-purpose prompts are easier to test and reuse in other pipelines.
  • Refer back explicitly. Phrases such as "the list above" and "your previous answer" help the model connect the steps.
  • Test steps one at a time. Run a prompt on its own, or with a context file that holds a sample of the previous step's output, before you add it to a chain.
  • Give parameters defaults if the pipeline will run unattended, for example from cron.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: A plugin is a Ruby file of helper methods and constants that you want every prompt to use. Put plugin files in your plugins directory, and AIA loads them at startup so their methods can be called from ERB in any prompt. During a chat session, AIA also reloads plugins as you edit them.

docs.title: Setting the plugins directory
docs.text:
AIA has no default plugins directory. Plugins load only after you set one. You can set it three ways. They are listed here from lowest to highest priority:

Config fileEnvironment variableCommand line 
# ~/.config/aia/aia.yml
paths:
  plugins_dir: ~/.prompts/plugins

export AIA_PLUGINS_DIR=~/.prompts/plugins

aia --plugins-dir ~/.prompts/plugins my_prompt

~ is expanded. If the directory you name doesn't exist, AIA prints Warning: configured plugins directory does not exist: ... and runs without plugins.

The environment variable name

Besides AIA_PATHS__PLUGINS_DIR, the form used by the other AIA_* settings, AIA also reads the shorter AIA_PLUGINS_DIR. If both are set, AIA_PLUGINS_DIR wins.

docs.title: What counts as a plugin
docs.text:
AIA loads every *.rb file directly inside the plugins directory. It doesn't look in subdirectories, so you can keep helper files or work in progress in a subfolder.

Each plugin file can define:

  • Top-level methods (def outside any class or module)
  • Top-level constants, classes and modules
# ~/.prompts/plugins/project.rb

TEAM = "Platform"

def today
  Time.now.strftime("%A, %B %-d %Y")
end

def recent_commits(count = 10)
  `git log --oneline -#{count}`.chomp
end

def file_or_empty(path)
  File.exist?(path) ? File.read(path) : ""
end

docs.title: Using plugin methods in prompts
docs.text:
Plugin methods and constants are available in ERB tags in every prompt file:

---
parameters:
  count: 5
---
Today is <%= today %>. Write a status update for the <%= TEAM %> team
based on these recent commits:

<%= recent_commits(count.to_i) %>

aia --plugins-dir ~/.prompts/plugins standup

AIA also renders chat input with ERB, so you can call plugin methods while you chat:

Follow up (cntl-D or 'exit' to end) #=>
Summarize <%= recent_commits(3) %>

The same methods can be called from the /ruby directive when it is enabled with --allow-ruby-eval. See ERB & Shell.

Plugin methods take priority over parameter names

If a plugin defines a method with the same name as one of a prompt's parameters, <%= name %> calls the plugin method and the parameter value is never used. The same applies to directives: a plugin method named include or webpage replaces that directive inside ERB. Give plugin methods distinctive names.

docs.title: Checking what is loaded
docs.text:
In a chat session, the /plugins directive lists the loaded plugins by file name (without .rb):

Follow up (cntl-D or 'exit' to end) #=>
/plugins

Loaded Plugins
==============
project

If nothing is loaded, it prints No plugins are loaded.

docs.title: Live reload during chat
docs.text:
When you start AIA with --chat, AIA watches the plugins directory for the whole session and applies changes as you save them:

You... AIA... Message (on STDERR) add a new *.rb file loads it Plugin loaded: name save changes to a plugin removes everything the old version defined, then loads the new version Plugin reloaded: name delete a plugin file removes the methods and constants it defined Plugin unloaded: name

Because AIA removes the old definitions before it reloads a file, a method you rename or delete in a plugin stops working right away and doesn't linger under its old name.

AIA uses native file system events to notice changes, so they show up almost instantly. If file events aren't available, it checks the directory once per second instead.

Live reload only runs in chat mode. In a normal one-shot run, AIA loads plugins once at startup.

docs.title: When a plugin fails to load
docs.text:
If a plugin raises an error or has a syntax error while loading, AIA prints a warning and continues without it:

Warning: Failed to load plugin '/Users/you/.prompts/plugins/project.rb': undefined local variable or method 'tody' for main

The other plugins still load. In chat mode, fix the file and save it, and AIA tries to load it again.

Plugins run as you

A plugin is ordinary Ruby that runs inside AIA with your user's permissions. It runs every time AIA starts. Only put files you wrote or trust in the plugins directory. See Security.

docs.title: Plugins compared with tools and directives
docs.text: You want... Use Helper methods or constants for your own prompt templates A plugin Something the model can decide to call while it answers A tool A /command you type in chat A directive

docs.title: Prompt Files
docs.text: A prompt file is a Markdown file that holds a prompt you want to reuse. You keep prompt files in your prompts directory and run one by naming it on the command line.

docs.title: Prompt IDs
docs.text:
The prompt ID is the file name without its .md extension. A file named ~/.prompts/code_review.md has the prompt ID code_review, and you run it like this:

aia code_review

AIA looks for <prompts dir>/<prompt ID>.md. If there is no such prompt and no file by that name either, AIA stops and suggests close matches. Here the prompt is code_review but a hyphen was typed:

No prompt named 'code-review' in /Users/you/.prompts (and no file by that name).
Did you mean: code_review?

Prompt IDs can include subfolders and hyphens: ~/.prompts/dev/code-review.md is dev/code-review. An ID that starts with /, ./, ../ or ~/ is a path to a prompt file anywhere on disk; .md is optional.

If the first argument names a file that exists in your current directory, AIA treats it as a context file rather than a prompt ID. Context files alone aren't enough to run: unless you add --chat (or the file is an executable prompt), AIA stops with A prompt ID is required…. See Context Files & Piping.

docs.title: The prompts directory
docs.text:
The default prompts directory is ~/.prompts. You can change it three ways. They are listed here from lowest to highest priority:

Config fileEnvironment variableCommand line 
# ~/.config/aia/aia.yml
prompts:
  dir: ~/work/prompts

export AIA_PROMPTS__DIR=~/work/prompts

aia --prompts-dir ~/work/prompts code_review

A typical layout looks like this:

~/.prompts/
├── code_review.md        # prompt IDs live at the top level
├── summarize.md
├── standup.md
├── roles/                # roles, used with --role
│   ├── ruby_expert.md
│   └── editor.md
├── skills/               # skills, used with --skill (one directory per skill)
│   └── changelog/
│       └── SKILL.md
├── tools/                # default directory for your own tools
└── _prompts.log          # AIA's prompt history log

Roles and skills are covered in Roles & Skills. Tools are covered in Tools.

docs.title: Anatomy of a prompt file
docs.text:
A prompt file has two parts. The first is an optional YAML front matter block between --- lines. The second is the body, the text that becomes the prompt.

---
parameters:
  language: Ruby
  focus: readability
---
<!-- Reviewer notes: keep this prompt short. HTML comments are removed. -->
You are reviewing <%= language %> code.
Concentrate on <%= focus %> and point out anything that will surprise
the next person who reads it.

Today is $(date +%A).

When you run it, AIA does the following:

  1. Removes HTML comments (<!-- ... -->), so you can leave notes for yourself in the file.
  2. Reads the front matter and applies its settings.
  3. Expands shell references such as $(date +%A) and $HOME.
  4. Renders ERB tags such as <%= language %>, and asks you for any required parameter values first.
  5. Adds the role in front, then adds skills, piped input and context files after the text. (In a chat session, skills go into the system prompt instead.)

Steps 3 and 4 are explained in ERB & Shell. Parameters are explained in Parameters.

docs.title: Front matter keys
docs.text:
AIA understands these keys at the top level of the front matter:

Key What it does Example parameters Declares the values the prompt needs. A null (empty) value means required. parameters: { name: null, tone: friendly } next Prompt ID to run after this one next: explain_joke pipeline List of prompt IDs to run after this one pipeline: [evaluate, pick_best] shell false turns off shell expansion for this file shell: false erb false turns off ERB rendering for this file erb: false config Any other AIA setting, nested the same way as in the config file see below

next and pipeline cannot both appear in one file. AIA stops with an error if they do.

Model settings (model, temperature, top_p, and llm: keys under config:) take effect before the prompt is sent. A different model: rebuilds the robot, carrying the conversation over as model_switch_history says; the other settings retune it in place. See Configuration Precedence.

docs.title: The config: section
docs.text:
Use config: for any setting that has no shortcut key. It takes the same nested keys as ~/.config/aia/aia.yml (see Config Keys):

---
config:
  flags:
    tokens: true
---
Summarize the attached file in five bullet points.

Don't set a value both ways. If a top-level key such as temperature: and the matching config: key are both in one file, AIA stops with a Conflict: error that names both keys.

docs.title: Other keys
docs.text:
AIA ignores any front matter key it doesn't recognize. That makes the front matter a good place for your own notes:

---
description: Weekly status report for the platform team
author: dewayne
---

Front matter settings are scoped to the run

Settings from front matter change AIA's configuration for the rest of the current run. They never change your config file.

docs.title: Finding prompts with fzf
docs.text:
Once you have a lot of prompts, you may not remember their exact names. Install fzf and use --fuzzy (-f) to choose a prompt interactively:

brew install fzf      # macOS
aia --fuzzy

fzf lists every prompt ID at the top level of your prompts directory and shows a preview of the highlighted file. Type to filter the list, press Enter to run the selected prompt, or press Esc to cancel.

--fuzzy works with other options too:

aia -f --model gpt-4o          # pick a prompt, run it with gpt-4o
aia -f --chat                  # pick a prompt, then keep chatting

If fzf isn't installed, aia --fuzzy stops with Error: 'fzf' is not installed. Please install 'fzf' to use the --fuzzy option.

docs.title: Writing a prompt step by step
docs.text:
1. Create the file:

    mkdir -p ~/.prompts
cat > ~/.prompts/commit_message.md <<'EOF'
Write a conventional commit message for the following staged diff.
Use a subject line under 60 characters, then a short body.

$(git diff --cached)
EOF

  2. Run it from inside a git repository with staged changes:

    aia --no-output commit_message

  3. Improve the wording and run it again. The prompt is plain text, so you can refine it as often as you like.

docs.title: Command-Line Options
docs.text: This page lists every option aia accepts, grouped the way aia --help groups them. For each one you get what it does, its default, the configuration key and environment variable that set the same thing, and an example.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
aia [options] [PROMPT_ID] [CONTEXT_FILE]*
aia [options] --chat [PROMPT_ID] [CONTEXT_FILE]*
  • PROMPT_ID is the name of a prompt file in your prompts directory, without the .md extension. aia code_review runs ~/.prompts/code_review.md; aia dev/code_review runs ~/.prompts/dev/code_review.md.
  • CONTEXT_FILE is any number of files whose contents are sent along with the prompt.
  • If the first argument is not a prompt ID, aia treats it as a context file. If that file starts with a #! line, aia runs it as an executable prompt.
  • Text piped on standard input is added to the prompt. With no prompt ID, piped text is the prompt.

You need a prompt ID unless you use --chat, --fuzzy, --pipeline (its first prompt runs first) or --role (the role file runs as the prompt), pipe the prompt in, or run an executable prompt. Context files on their own are not enough:

$ aia
A prompt ID is required unless you use --chat, --fuzzy, --pipeline or --role, pipe the prompt in, or run an executable prompt. Context files alone are not a prompt. Use -h or --help for help.

Option values

An option that takes a list (--pipeline, --skill, --tools, --allowed-tools, --mcp-use …) takes it comma-separated, with no spaces unless you quote it. Options that add to a list (-m, -s, -n, -p, --rq, --at, --rt, --mcp, --mu, --ms) can be repeated.

Reading the tables

Config key is the dotted path in ~/.config/aia/aia.yml (see Configuration Keys). Env is the matching environment variable (see Environment Variables). A dash means the option has no persistent equivalent.

docs.title: --chat
docs.text:
Start an interactive chat session. If you also give a prompt ID (or a pipeline), aia runs it first and then keeps the conversation open. See Chat Sessions.

Default Config key Env off flags.chat AIA_FLAGS__CHAT 
aia --chat
aia --chat code_review lib/parser.rb

docs.title: -f, --fuzzy
docs.text:
Pick the prompt interactively with fzf. aia stops immediately if fzf is not installed:

$ aia --fuzzy
Error: 'fzf' is not installed. Please install 'fzf' to use the --fuzzy option.
Default Config key Env off flags.fuzzy AIA_FLAGS__FUZZY 
aia -f
aia --fuzzy --chat

docs.title: --track-pipeline
docs.text:
Record each step of a pipeline as a task in TrakFlow. It only takes effect when the current directory holds an initialized TrakFlow project; otherwise the pipeline runs untracked.

Default Config key Env off flags.track_pipeline AIA_FLAGS__TRACK_PIPELINE 
aia --track-pipeline research -p outline,draft

docs.title: --concurrent-auto
docs.text:
Run MCP servers that can work independently of each other in parallel, without asking for it turn by turn (the per-turn form is the /concurrent directive). Parallelism kicks in only when there are at least concurrency.threshold independent groups (default 2). See MCP Servers.

Default Config key Env off concurrency.auto AIA_CONCURRENCY__AUTO

docs.title: -A, --[no-]auto-tool-filter
docs.text:
Before each turn, offer the model only the tools whose descriptions are similar to your prompt (TF-IDF similarity). Turn it off with --no-auto-tool-filter to offer every loaded tool on every turn.

Default Config key Env on flags.auto_tool_filter AIA_FLAGS__AUTO_TOOL_FILTER 
aia --chat --no-auto-tool-filter --tools ~/my_tools

docs.title: --available-models [QUERY]
docs.text:
Search the model registry and exit. With no query it lists every known model. The query is comma-separated; every term must match. A term containing _to_ filters by modality (text_to_image, audio_to_text …); any other term must appear in the model's line.

$ aia --available-models claude-haiku
Available LLMs for claude-haiku:

- claude-haiku-4-5 (anthropic) text,image,pdf to text
- claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (anthropic) text,image,pdf to text
...

aia --available-models anthropic,text_to_text
aia --available-models text_to_image

This option exits as soon as it is parsed, so put it last if you combine it with other options.

docs.title: --provider SLUG
docs.text:
The provider to use for model names given without a provider/ prefix. It also selects the provider for --list-models. A model written with an explicit prefix (ollama/llama3.2) keeps its own provider. Run aia --list-providers to see the valid slugs.

Default Config key Env none (the model registry decides) — — 
aia --provider ollama -m llama3.2 my_prompt
aia --provider lms --list-models

docs.title: --list-models
docs.text:
List the models a provider is serving right now (it asks the provider, so a local server must be running) and exit. Requires --provider.

$ aia --list-models
ERROR: --list-models requires --provider SLUG (use --available-models to search the full model registry)

aia --provider ollama --list-models

docs.title: --list-providers
docs.text:
List every provider aia can use and exit. Each line notes (local) for providers that run on your machine and (has API key) when a key for it is set.

$ aia --list-providers

Registered RubyLLM providers:
------------------------------------------------------------
- anthropic
- gemini (has API key)
- ollama (local)
- openai
...

21 provider(s) registered

Provider gems named ruby_llm-providers-<slug> that are installed are loaded automatically and appear here. Libraries named with --require are loaded first, so a provider they register is listed too.

docs.title: -m, --model MODEL
docs.text:
The model, or models, to use. Format: MODEL[=ROLE][,MODEL[=ROLE]]...

  • One model: -m claude-haiku-4-5
  • With an explicit provider: -m ollama/llama3.2
  • Several models run the same prompt in parallel: -m gpt-4o,claude-sonnet-4-6. See Multi-Model & Consensus.
  • =ROLE gives that model its own role: -m gpt-4o=architect,claude-sonnet-4-6=reviewer. The role file must exist, or aia stops with ERROR: Role file not found and lists the roles it found.
  • The same model can appear more than once, with different roles.
Default Config key Env gpt-4o-mini models AIA_MODEL (comma-separated) 
aia -m claude-sonnet-4-6 summarize report.pdf
aia -m gpt-4o=optimist,gpt-4o=pessimist --consensus forecast

docs.title: --[no-]consensus
docs.text:
With several models, have one more pass merge their answers into a single response instead of showing each answer separately.

Default Config key Env off flags.consensus AIA_FLAGS__CONSENSUS 
aia -m gpt-4o,claude-sonnet-4-6,gemini-2.5-pro --consensus architecture_question

docs.title: --list-roles
docs.text:
List the role files in your roles directory, with each role's front matter, and exit. Hidden files and directories whose names start with _ are skipped.

aia --list-roles

docs.title: --sm, --speech-model MODEL
docs.text:
The text-to-speech model. aia passes it to your speak command as the SPEECH_MODEL environment variable. See Images & Speech.

Default Config key Env none audio.speech_model AIA_AUDIO__SPEECH_MODEL

docs.title: --tm, --transcription-model MODEL
docs.text:
The speech-to-text model used for the whole session.

Default Config key Env none (provider default) audio.transcription_model AIA_AUDIO__TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL

docs.title: -c, --config-file FILE
docs.text:
Load settings from FILE instead of your personal configuration. When you use it, aia starts from its built-in defaults, applies FILE, then your command-line options — ~/.config/aia/aia.yml, a project ./config/aia.yml and AIA_* environment variables are not used. (AIA_MODEL and AIA_PLUGINS_DIR are the exceptions; they still apply.) See Configuration Precedence.

$ aia -c missing.yml my_prompt
ERROR: Config file not found: /home/you/missing.yml

aia -c ~/configs/local-ollama.yml --chat

docs.title: -o, --[no-]output [FILE]
docs.text:
Where the response is written, in addition to the terminal. Given without a file name, it means temp.md. A relative path is relative to the current directory. --no-output turns file output off.

Default Config key Env temp.md output.file AIA_OUTPUT__FILE 
aia -o review.md code_review lib/app.rb
aia --no-output quick_question

Tip

Because the default is temp.md, every run leaves a temp.md in your current directory. Set output.file: false in your config file, or pass --no-output, if you don't want that. (output.file: ~ does not work: a null in your config file is ignored and the default stays.)

docs.title: -a, --[no-]append
docs.text:
Add each response to the end of the output file instead of replacing it. Without it, aia empties the output file at the start of a session.

Default Config key Env off output.append AIA_OUTPUT__APPEND 
aia -a -o journal.md daily_reflection

docs.title: --[no-]history-file [FILE]
docs.text:
The file that holds the lines you type at the chat prompt, so the up-arrow recalls earlier input across sessions (the last 50 lines are loaded). When it grows past 10 MB aia renames it to FILE.1 and starts a new one. --no-history-file turns chat input history off.

Default Config key Env ~/.prompts/_prompts.log output.history_file AIA_OUTPUT__HISTORY_FILE 
aia --chat --history-file ~/.config/aia/chat_history
aia --chat --no-history-file

docs.title: --prompts-dir DIR
docs.text:
The directory that holds your prompt files.

Default Config key Env ~/.prompts prompts.dir AIA_PROMPTS__DIR 
aia --prompts-dir ./prompts release_notes

docs.title: --plugins-dir DIR
docs.text:
A directory of Ruby plugin files. Every *.rb file directly inside it is loaded at startup; during a chat session aia watches the directory and reloads a plugin when you add, change or delete it. aia warns if the directory does not exist. See Plugins.

Default Config key Env none paths.plugins_dir AIA_PLUGINS_DIR 
aia --chat --plugins-dir ~/.config/aia/plugins

docs.title: --roles-prefix PREFIX
docs.text:
The subdirectory of the prompts directory that holds role files.

Default Config key Env roles prompts.roles_prefix AIA_PROMPTS__ROLES_PREFIX

docs.title: -r, --role ROLE_ID
docs.text:
Put a role in front of the prompt. ROLE_ID is a file in the roles directory (-r ruby_expert reads ~/.prompts/roles/ruby_expert.md) or a path to a file (-r ./roles/reviewer.md). With --chat, the role becomes part of the session's system prompt. Outside chat you still need a prompt ID: aia -r tutor on its own stops with A prompt ID is required …. See Roles & Skills.

Default Config key Env none prompts.role AIA_PROMPTS__ROLE 
aia -r ruby_expert code_review app/models/user.rb
aia --chat -r tutor

docs.title: --skills-dir DIR
docs.text:
The directory whose subdirectories are skills (each one holds a SKILL.md).

Default Config key Env ~/.prompts/skills skills.dir AIA_SKILLS__DIR

docs.title: -s, --skill SKILL_IDS
docs.text:
Add one or more skills, comma-separated, by name or by path. In chat mode the skills are added to the system prompt once, for the whole session. When running prompts, they are added to each prompt. See Roles & Skills.

Default Config key Env none prompts.skills — 
aia --chat -s code_review,security_audit
aia -s ./skills/house_style summarize notes.md

docs.title: --list-skills
docs.text:
List the skills in the skills directory and exit.

aia --list-skills
aia --skills-dir ./team_skills --list-skills

docs.title: -n, --next PROMPT_ID
docs.text:
Run PROMPT_ID after the current prompt. Pipeline prompts share one conversation, so each one sees the prompts and responses before it. Repeat -n to chain more. See Pipelines.

Default Config key Env none pipeline AIA_PIPELINE (comma-separated) 
aia extract_facts report.pdf -n summarize -n translate_es

docs.title: -p, --pipeline PROMPTS
docs.text:
Run a comma-separated list of prompts in order. The prompt ID you give on the command line runs first; you need one unless you also use --chat. Every prompt in the list must exist before anything runs:

$ aia research -p outline,draftt
Error: Prompt ID 'draftt' does not exist at /home/you/.prompts/draftt.md
One or more prompt IDs do not exist.
Default Config key Env [] pipeline AIA_PIPELINE (comma-separated) 
aia research -p outline,draft topic_notes.md

docs.title: --system-prompt TEXT
docs.text:
Use TEXT as the system prompt, in chat and in one-shot runs. The value is literal text; aia doesn't look up a prompt file. A role (--role) is added after it.

aia --system-prompt "Answer in one short paragraph." my_prompt
Default Config key Env none prompts.system_prompt AIA_PROMPTS__SYSTEM_PROMPT 
# ~/.config/aia/aia.yml
prompts:
  system_prompt: |
    Answer in British English.
    Keep answers under 200 words.

docs.title: Generation Parameters
docs.text: These are passed to the model. Not every model honors every one.

docs.title: -t, --temperature TEMP
docs.text:
Randomness of the output; lower is more focused, higher more varied. Must be a number.

Default Config key Env 0.7 llm.temperature AIA_LLM__TEMPERATURE 
aia -t 0.2 extract_dates contract.txt

docs.title: --max-tokens TOKENS
docs.text:
Upper limit on the length of the response, in tokens. Must be an integer.

Default Config key Env 32767 llm.max_tokens AIA_LLM__MAX_TOKENS

docs.title: --top-p VALUE
docs.text:
Nucleus sampling. Unset by default, because some models reject a request that sets both temperature and top_p.

Default Config key Env unset llm.top_p AIA_LLM__TOP_P

docs.title: --frequency-penalty VALUE
docs.text:
Discourages repeating the same tokens.

Default Config key Env 0.0 llm.frequency_penalty AIA_LLM__FREQUENCY_PENALTY

docs.title: --presence-penalty VALUE
docs.text:
Encourages moving on to new topics.

Default Config key Env 0.0 llm.presence_penalty AIA_LLM__PRESENCE_PENALTY

A value that is not a number stops aia with an invalid argument error, for example invalid argument: -t hot.

docs.title: Audio & Image Options
docs.text: See Images & Speech for walkthroughs.

docs.title: --speak
docs.text:
Speak each response aloud after it is shown: every reply in a chat, the reply to a one-shot prompt, and each step of a pipeline. --paint results aren't spoken. See Images & Speech.

Default Config key Env off flags.speak AIA_FLAGS__SPEAK 
aia --speak --chat

docs.title: --voice VOICE
docs.text:
The voice. With the default speak command (say), it is passed as say -v VOICE.

Default Config key Env none audio.voice AIA_AUDIO__VOICE 
aia --speak --voice Samantha daily_briefing

docs.title: --speak-command CMD
docs.text:
The program that speaks. With say, aia calls say [-v VOICE] TEXT. Any other command is called as CMD TEXT OUTFILE; it must write an audio file to OUTFILE, which aia then plays with your audio player (audio.player; see config-keys). The speech model is in $SPEECH_MODEL.

Default Config key Env say audio.speak_command AIA_AUDIO__SPEAK_COMMAND 
aia --speak --speak-command ~/bin/openai_tts.sh --speech-model tts-1-hd my_prompt

docs.title: --paint
docs.text:
Generate an image from the prompt instead of a text response. The image is saved next to the output file with a .png extension; the output file itself isn't written, and nothing is spoken.

Default Config key Env off flags.paint AIA_FLAGS__PAINT 
aia --paint logo_idea

docs.title: --im, --image-model MODEL
docs.text: Default Config key Env gpt-image-1 image.model AIA_IMAGE__MODEL

docs.title: --is, --image-size SIZE
docs.text: Default Config key Env 1024x1024 image.size AIA_IMAGE__SIZE

docs.title: --iq, --image-quality QUALITY
docs.text: Default Config key Env standard image.quality AIA_IMAGE__QUALITY

docs.title: --style, --image-style STYLE
docs.text:
Default Config key Env vivid image.style AIA_IMAGE__STYLE 
aia --paint --is 1792x1024 --iq hd --style natural landscape

docs.title: --allow-ruby-eval
docs.text:
Turn on the /ruby directive, which runs arbitrary Ruby code with aia's full privileges. Read Security first.

Default Config key Env off flags.allow_ruby_eval AIA_FLAGS__ALLOW_RUBY_EVAL

docs.title: --rq, --require LIBS
docs.text:
Ruby libraries (gems) to load at startup, comma-separated. Use it to load tool gems, provider gems, or code your prompts call. A library that can't be loaded produces a warning, not an error.

Default Config key Env [] require_libs AIA_REQUIRE_LIBS (comma-separated) 
aia --rq shared_tools --chat

docs.title: --tools PATH_LIST
docs.text:
Load tools from Ruby files. Each entry is a .rb file or a directory (every *.rb file in it is loaded). aia stops if a path does not exist or a file is not .rb:

$ aia --tools README my_prompt
file/dir path is not valid: README
Default Config key Env [] tools.paths AIA_TOOLS__PATHS 
aia --chat --tools ~/my_tools,./project_tools/deploy_tool.rb

See Tools.

docs.title: --at, --allowed-tools TOOLS_LIST
docs.text:
Offer the model only the tools whose names contain one of these strings (case-insensitive, substring match — --at file keeps read_file, write_file and file_search).

Default Config key Env all tools.allowed AIA_TOOLS__ALLOWED

docs.title: --rt, --rejected-tools TOOLS_LIST
docs.text:
Remove the tools whose names contain one of these strings (same matching as --at). Rejection is applied after --at.

Default Config key Env none tools.rejected AIA_TOOLS__REJECTED 
aia --chat --rq shared_tools --rt delete,shell

docs.title: --tool-approval MODE
docs.text:
What to do with tool calls that need approval (tools from an MCP server marked requires_approval:) and with an MCP server's requests for input:

  • ask — show the tool and its arguments and ask Allow it? [y/N] on the terminal. With no terminal attached, the call is refused.
  • approve — allow them all without asking.
  • deny — refuse them all.
Default Config key Env ask tools.approval AIA_TOOLS__APPROVAL 
aia --tool-approval deny nightly_report

Any other value stops aia with invalid argument: --tool-approval ….

docs.title: --list-tools
docs.text:
List the local tools (from --tools and --require) with their descriptions, after --allowed-tools and --rejected-tools are applied, and exit. Add --mcp-list to connect to each MCP server and list its tools as well. When output is not a terminal, the list is written as Markdown.

aia --tools ~/my_tools --list-tools
aia --list-tools --mcp-list > tools.md

docs.title: --log-level LEVEL
docs.text:
Set the level of all three logs (aia, LLM, MCP) to debug, info, warn, error or fatal. debug also turns on --debug.

aia --log-level info my_prompt

The level for each log can be set separately in the config file; see logger.* in Configuration Keys.

docs.title: -d, --debug
docs.text:
Debug output: the same as --log-level debug. Also shows which tools were offered to the model on each turn.

Default Config key Env off flags.debug AIA_FLAGS__DEBUG

docs.title: --no-debug
docs.text: Turn debug output off, overriding a config file or environment setting.

docs.title: --log-to FILE
docs.text:
Send all three logs to FILE instead of their configured destinations.

aia --debug --log-to /tmp/aia.log --chat

docs.title: -v, --[no-]verbose
docs.text:
Print extra detail, such as the list of tools offered to the model on each turn.

Default Config key Env off flags.verbose AIA_FLAGS__VERBOSE

docs.title: --[no-]thinking
docs.text:
Show the reasoning that some models (for example qwen3 on Ollama) stream inside <think>…</think> tags. By default aia hides it and shows only the answer.

Default Config key Env off flags.thinking AIA_FLAGS__THINKING

docs.title: --tokens
docs.text:
After each turn, show the tokens used and how long the response took.

Default Config key Env off flags.tokens AIA_FLAGS__TOKENS

docs.title: --cost
docs.text:
Show the cost of each turn as well as tokens and time. Implies --tokens. In chat, /cost prints the session's totals as CSV.

Default Config key Env off flags.cost AIA_FLAGS__COST 
aia --cost -m gpt-4o,claude-sonnet-4-6 compare_designs

docs.title: --refresh DAYS
docs.text:
How often, in days, AIA refreshes its list of models. AIA keeps the list in models.json in its own directory (paths.aia_dir, ~/.config/aia by default). When a session starts and the file is missing or more than DAYS days old, AIA asks the providers you have API keys for and the published RubyLLM catalogue for their current models, and saves the result. 0 turns refreshing off; AIA then uses the saved file if there is one, or the list that comes with RubyLLM. If the refresh fails (for example, offline), AIA warns and carries on with the list it already had.

The chat banner's DB: line shows when the list was last refreshed. /models searches this list. --available-models runs before the session starts, so it searches the list RubyLLM keeps for itself.

aia --refresh 0 --chat     # never refresh
aia --refresh 1 --chat     # refresh at most once a day
Default Config key Env 7 registry.refresh AIA_REGISTRY__REFRESH

docs.title: --dump FILE
docs.text:
Write the complete configuration aia would run with — after config files, environment variables and the other options on the command line — to FILE and exit. FILE must end in .yml or .yaml.

$ aia --dump current.yml
Config successfully dumped to current.yml

This is the quickest way to answer "where did that setting come from?". See The Config File.

docs.title: --completion SHELL
docs.text:
Print a tab-completion script for bash, zsh or fish and exit. Any other shell name is an error (exit status 1). The script completes prompt IDs after aia by listing the .md files under $AIA_PROMPTS__DIR, or ~/.prompts when that variable is unset. The script can't read your config file, so if your prompts live elsewhere, export AIA_PROMPTS__DIR. Elsewhere on the command line it falls back to ordinary file completion.

bashzshfish 
# ~/.bashrc
export AIA_PROMPTS__DIR=~/.prompts
eval "$(aia --completion bash)"

# ~/.zshrc
export AIA_PROMPTS__DIR=~/.prompts
eval "$(aia --completion zsh)"

# ~/.config/fish/config.fish
set -gx AIA_PROMPTS__DIR ~/.prompts
aia --completion fish | source

$ aia --completion tcsh
ERROR: The shell 'tcsh' is not supported or the completion script is missing.

docs.title: --mcp FILE
docs.text:
Add MCP servers from a JSON file. Repeat it to load several files. The file can describe a single server (named after the file) or hold an mcpServers object, the format used by Claude Desktop and other MCP clients. A missing or malformed file produces a warning and is skipped. See MCP Servers.

Default Config key Env none adds to mcp_servers — 
aia --chat --mcp ~/mcp/github.json --mcp ~/mcp/filesystem.json

docs.title: --no-mcp
docs.text:
Don't connect to any MCP server, even ones in your config file.

Default Config key Env off flags.no_mcp AIA_FLAGS__NO_MCP

docs.title: --mcp-list
docs.text:
List the configured MCP servers (after --mcp-use / --mcp-skip filtering) and exit. Combine with --list-tools to also list each server's tools.

$ aia --mcp-list
Configured MCP servers:

  github
    command: github-mcp-server stdio

  filesystem
    command: npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /Users/you/projects

docs.title: --mu, --mcp-use NAMES
docs.text:
Use only these MCP servers (comma-separated names). aia warns about names that are not configured.

Default Config key Env all mcp_use AIA_MCP_USE (comma-separated)

docs.title: --ms, --mcp-skip NAMES
docs.text:
Use every configured MCP server except these. Ignored when --mcp-use is given.

Default Config key Env none mcp_skip AIA_MCP_SKIP (comma-separated) 
aia --chat --mu github
aia --chat --ms slow_db_server

docs.title: --version
docs.text:
Print the version and exit.

$ aia --version
2.0.0

docs.title: -h, --help
docs.text: Print the option summary and exit.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: aia exits with status 1 for an unknown option, a missing or invalid value (-t hot, --tool-approval maybe), a -m MODEL=ROLE whose role file is missing, a configuration error (such as a missing prompt or config file), or a failed --list-models. Each prints a one-line ERROR: message.

docs.text:
