  • Environment Variables
  • Configuration Precedence
  • Directives — commands you use inside prompts and chat

docs.title: Configuration Keys
docs.text:
Every setting aia understands, section by section, with its type, default, environment variable and command-line option. The defaults shown are the ones built into aia 2.0.0.

Settings are written in YAML in ~/.config/aia/aia.yml (see The Config File). In this page a key is written as a dotted path: llm.temperature means

llm:
  temperature: 0.7

The environment variable for a key is AIA_ followed by the path in capitals, with __ (two underscores) between levels: llm.temperature → AIA_LLM__TEMPERATURE. Read Environment Variables before using them for true/false settings.

To see the value of every key as aia will actually use it, run aia --dump current.yml.

Keys with no effect in 2.0.0

A few keys are still part of the configuration schema but nothing in aia 2.0.0 reads them. They are marked No effect below. Setting them does no harm, but don't expect a change.

docs.title: llm — generation parameters
docs.text:
Key Type Default Env CLI Meaning llm.temperature float 0.7 AIA_LLM__TEMPERATURE -t Randomness of the response. llm.max_tokens integer 32767 AIA_LLM__MAX_TOKENS --max-tokens Maximum length of the response. llm.top_p float unset AIA_LLM__TOP_P --top-p Nucleus sampling. Left unset because some models reject temperature and top_p together. llm.frequency_penalty float 0.0 AIA_LLM__FREQUENCY_PENALTY --frequency-penalty Penalizes repeated tokens. llm.presence_penalty float 0.0 AIA_LLM__PRESENCE_PENALTY --presence-penalty Encourages new topics.

A prompt's front matter can set temperature and top_p for that prompt. See Prompt Files.

docs.title: models — which model(s) to use
docs.text:
A list. Each entry has a name and an optional role.

Key Type Default Env CLI models list of {name, role} [{name: gpt-4o-mini}] AIA_MODEL -m, --model 
models:
  - name: claude-sonnet-4-6
  - name: ollama/llama3.2      # provider prefix
    role: reviewer             # a file in your roles directory
  • A name can carry a provider prefix (ollama/llama3.2, lms/qwen3). The prefix is treated as a provider only if aia knows that provider; otherwise the whole string is the model name (as in meta-llama/llama-4-maverick on OpenRouter).
  • More than one entry runs every prompt on every model. See Multi-Model & Consensus.
  • AIA_MODEL takes the same comma-separated form as -m: AIA_MODEL=gpt-4o,claude-sonnet-4-6.

docs.title: prompts — where prompts, roles and skills come from
docs.text: Key Type Default Env CLI Meaning prompts.dir path ~/.prompts AIA_PROMPTS__DIR --prompts-dir Directory of prompt files. prompts.extname string .md AIA_PROMPTS__EXTNAME — File extension of prompt files. prompts.role string unset AIA_PROMPTS__ROLE -r, --role Role to apply. A role ID or a path to a file. prompts.roles_prefix string roles AIA_PROMPTS__ROLES_PREFIX --roles-prefix Subdirectory of prompts.dir holding role files. prompts.skills list [] — -s, --skill Skills to add to every prompt or chat session. prompts.system_prompt string unset AIA_PROMPTS__SYSTEM_PROMPT --system-prompt System prompt text, used in chat and one-shot runs. Literal text, not a prompt ID.

docs.title: skills
docs.text: Key Type Default Env CLI Meaning skills.dir path ~/.prompts/skills AIA_SKILLS__DIR --skills-dir Directory whose subdirectories are skills. It does not follow prompts.dir; set it too if you move your prompts.

docs.title: output — files aia writes
docs.text: Key Type Default Env CLI Meaning output.file path or false temp.md AIA_OUTPUT__FILE -o, --no-output Where responses (and, in chat, your messages) are written as well as shown. false turns it off. output.append boolean false AIA_OUTPUT__APPEND -a, --append Add to output.file instead of emptying it at the start of a session. output.history_file path ~/.prompts/_prompts.log AIA_OUTPUT__HISTORY_FILE --history-file, --no-history-file Chat input history (up-arrow recall). Rotated to <file>.1 past 10 MB.

docs.title: audio — speech
docs.text:
Key Type Default Env CLI Meaning audio.voice string unset AIA_AUDIO__VOICE --voice Voice name, passed to say -v. audio.speak_command string say AIA_AUDIO__SPEAK_COMMAND --speak-command Program that speaks responses. Other than say, it is called as CMD TEXT OUTFILE and the resulting file is played with audio.player. audio.player string unset AIA_AUDIO__PLAYER — Command that plays the file a custom speak command writes, e.g. mpv --no-video. Unset: the first of afplay, mpv, ffplay, mpg123 found on your PATH. audio.speech_model string unset AIA_AUDIO__SPEECH_MODEL --speech-model Passed to the speak command as $SPEECH_MODEL. audio.transcription_model string unset AIA_AUDIO__TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL --transcription-model Speech-to-text model for the session.

Turning speech on is a flag: flags.speak.

docs.title: image — image generation
docs.text:
Key Type Default Env CLI image.model string gpt-image-1 AIA_IMAGE__MODEL --image-model image.size string 1024x1024 AIA_IMAGE__SIZE --image-size image.quality string standard AIA_IMAGE__QUALITY --image-quality image.style string vivid AIA_IMAGE__STYLE --image-style

Turning image generation on is a flag: flags.paint (--paint). See Images & Speech.

docs.title: tools — local tools
docs.text:
Key Type Default Env CLI Meaning tools.paths list of paths [] AIA_TOOLS__PATHS --tools Ruby files to load as tools. In the config file list files, not directories (--tools expands directories for you). tools.allowed list unset (all) AIA_TOOLS__ALLOWED --allowed-tools Keep only tools whose name contains one of these strings. tools.rejected list unset AIA_TOOLS__REJECTED --rejected-tools Drop tools whose name contains one of these strings. tools.approval ask | approve | deny ask AIA_TOOLS__APPROVAL --tool-approval How to handle tool calls that need approval and MCP input requests. See Security.

Note

In an environment variable, separate list items with commas: AIA_TOOLS__ALLOWED=read,write, AIA_TOOLS__PATHS=~/tools/a.rb,~/tools/b.rb.

docs.title: flags — on/off switches
docs.text: Key Default Env CLI Meaning flags.chat false AIA_FLAGS__CHAT --chat Start a chat session. flags.cost false AIA_FLAGS__COST --cost Show cost per turn. flags.debug false AIA_FLAGS__DEBUG -d, --debug Debug output. flags.verbose false AIA_FLAGS__VERBOSE -v Extra detail. flags.fuzzy false AIA_FLAGS__FUZZY -f Choose the prompt with fzf. flags.tokens false AIA_FLAGS__TOKENS --tokens Show tokens and elapsed time per turn. flags.no_mcp false AIA_FLAGS__NO_MCP --no-mcp Don't connect to MCP servers. flags.speak false AIA_FLAGS__SPEAK --speak Speak responses. flags.shell true AIA_FLAGS__SHELL — Expand $(...) and $VAR in prompts. A prompt's shell: front matter overrides it. flags.erb true AIA_FLAGS__ERB — Render ERB (<%= %>) in prompts. A prompt's erb: front matter overrides it. flags.consensus false AIA_FLAGS__CONSENSUS --consensus Merge multi-model answers into one. flags.track_pipeline false AIA_FLAGS__TRACK_PIPELINE --track-pipeline Track pipelines in TrakFlow. flags.auto_tool_filter true AIA_FLAGS__AUTO_TOOL_FILTER -A, --[no-]auto-tool-filter Offer only tools relevant to the prompt. flags.allow_ruby_eval false AIA_FLAGS__ALLOW_RUBY_EVAL --allow-ruby-eval Enable the /ruby directive. flags.paint false AIA_FLAGS__PAINT --paint Generate images instead of text. flags.thinking false AIA_FLAGS__THINKING --[no-]thinking Show <think> reasoning blocks.

docs.title: tool_filter
docs.text: Key Type Default Env Meaning tool_filter.timeout_s number 10 AIA_TOOL_FILTER__TIMEOUT_S Seconds the chat tool filter may take per turn before it is skipped.

docs.title: logger — log destinations and levels
docs.text:
aia keeps three logs: aia (aia itself), llm (requests to the model) and mcp (MCP connections).

Key Type Default Env logger.aia.file STDOUT, STDERR or a path STDOUT AIA_LOGGER__AIA__FILE logger.aia.level debug … fatal warn AIA_LOGGER__AIA__LEVEL logger.aia.flush boolean true AIA_LOGGER__AIA__FLUSH logger.llm.file as above STDOUT AIA_LOGGER__LLM__FILE logger.llm.level as above warn AIA_LOGGER__LLM__LEVEL logger.llm.flush boolean true AIA_LOGGER__LLM__FLUSH logger.mcp.file as above STDOUT AIA_LOGGER__MCP__FILE logger.mcp.level as above warn AIA_LOGGER__MCP__LEVEL logger.mcp.flush boolean true AIA_LOGGER__MCP__FLUSH

--log-level and --log-to override the level and file of all three at once. flush: true writes each entry immediately.

logger:
  llm:
    file: ~/.config/aia/logs/llm.log
    level: info

docs.title: pipeline
docs.text:
Key Type Default Env CLI pipeline list of prompt IDs [] AIA_PIPELINE -p, -n

Prompts to run in order. Usually given on the command line or in a prompt's front matter (next: / pipeline:). See Pipelines.

docs.title: registry
docs.text: Key Type Default Env CLI Meaning registry.refresh integer (days) 7 AIA_REGISTRY__REFRESH --refresh Days between refreshes of the model list in <paths.aia_dir>/models.json. 0 never refreshes. See --refresh.

docs.title: require_libs
docs.text:
Key Type Default Env CLI require_libs list of gem/library names [] AIA_REQUIRE_LIBS (comma-separated) --rq, --require

Libraries loaded at startup — tool gems such as shared_tools, provider gems, or code your prompts use.

docs.title: mcp_servers, mcp_use, mcp_skip
docs.text:
Key Type Default Env CLI mcp_servers list of server definitions [] — --mcp FILE adds to it mcp_use list of server names unset (all) AIA_MCP_USE (comma-separated) --mu, --mcp-use mcp_skip list of server names unset AIA_MCP_SKIP (comma-separated) --ms, --mcp-skip 
mcp_servers:
  - name: filesystem
    command: npx
    args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "~/projects"]
  - name: docs
    url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
    requires_approval: true

Each server has a name and either a command (with args, env) for a local stdio server or a url (with headers or bearer_token) for a Streamable HTTP server. Optional keys include prefix, only, except, requires_approval, description and timeout. All of them are explained in MCP Servers.

docs.title: paths
docs.text: Key Type Default Env CLI Meaning paths.aia_dir path ~/.config/aia AIA_PATHS__AIA_DIR — aia's own directory. It holds the model list (models.json). Chat history falls back to <aia_dir>/chat_history when output.history_file is unset. paths.plugins_dir path unset AIA_PLUGINS_DIR --plugins-dir Directory of Ruby plugin files. See Plugins.

docs.title: model_aliases, model_switch_history
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning model_aliases map {} Extra short names for /model, e.g. writer: claude-sonnet-4-5. Added to the built-in aliases (sonnet, haiku, gpt4o, cheap, fast …). model_switch_history clean | replay | summarize summarize What the new model gets when you switch models: a summary, every message re-sent, or nothing. Env: AIA_MODEL_SWITCH_HISTORY.

docs.title: concurrency — parallel MCP servers
docs.text: Key Type Default Env CLI Meaning concurrency.auto boolean false AIA_CONCURRENCY__AUTO --concurrent-auto Run independent MCP servers in parallel on every turn. concurrency.threshold integer 2 AIA_CONCURRENCY__THRESHOLD — Minimum number of independent server groups before running them in parallel. concurrency.mcp_timeout integer (seconds) 120 AIA_CONCURRENCY__MCP_TIMEOUT — Overall time allowed for connecting to all MCP servers at startup. Servers not connected by then are reported as failed and left out.

docs.title: context_files
docs.text:
Key Type Default Env context_files list of paths [] AIA_CONTEXT_FILES

The context files for the run. aia fills it from the file names on the command line; anything you put here is sent in addition.

docs.title: service
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning service.name string aia Internal identifier. Leave it alone.

docs.title: Front matter vs. config keys
docs.text:
A prompt's YAML front matter can change configuration for the run. The short forms model, temperature, top_p, next, pipeline, shell and erb sit at the top level; anything else goes under a config: section using the same section names as this page:

---
config:
  output:
    file: review.md
  flags:
    tokens: true
---

Setting the same thing both ways (say temperature: and config.llm.temperature:) is an error, as is using both next: and pipeline:. See Prompt Files.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• The Config File
  • Environment Variables
  • Configuration Precedence
  • Command-Line Options

docs.title: Directives Reference
docs.text: This page lists every directive in AIA 2.0 in alphabetical order, with its aliases, arguments and an example. For an introduction, read Directives first.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
Where Form Notes Chat /name arg1 arg2 Must be on a line by itself. The name is case-insensitive. Arguments are split on spaces, and quotes don't group words. Prompt file <%= name 'arg1', 'arg2' %> An ERB tag. Its result replaces the tag. A directive with no arguments is just <%= name %>.

Use in shows where each directive is meant to be used:

  • Chat: designed for interactive sessions.
  • Prompt: returns text, so it is useful inside a prompt file.
  • Both: useful in either place.

Chat output describes what happens to the result in a chat session:

  • Sent: AIA prints the result and also sends it to the model as part of the conversation.
  • Shown: AIA prints the result only. Nothing reaches the model.
  • Next prompt: AIA turns on a mode that applies to your next message only.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Directive Aliases Use in Chat output Purpose /add_recruit /add Chat Shown Add a persistent robot to the crew /available_models /am, /available, /models, /all_models, /llms Chat Shown Search the model list /checkpoint /ckp, /cp Chat Shown Save a point in the conversation /checkpoints_list /checkpoints Chat Shown List checkpoints /clear Chat Shown Forget the conversation /compare /cmp Chat Shown Ask several models the same thing /concurrent /conc Chat Next prompt Query MCP server groups in parallel /config /cfg Chat Shown Show or change settings /cost Chat Shown Token and cost report as CSV /debate Chat Next prompt Multi-round debate between robots /decompose Chat Next prompt Split a prompt into parallel sub-tasks /delegate /del Chat Next prompt Assign sub-tasks to robots via TrakFlow /drop_recruit /drop Chat Shown Remove a robot from the crew /help Chat Shown List all directives /include Both Sent Insert another file, processed as a prompt /insert /read Both Sent Insert a file's raw text /mcp Chat Shown MCP server status and tools /model Chat Shown Show or switch the model /orchestrate /orch Chat Next prompt Three-tier orchestration /paste /clipboard Both Sent Insert the clipboard contents /plan Chat Sent Create a TrakFlow plan /plugins Chat Shown List loaded plugins /reskill Chat Shown Reset a crew member with new skills /restore Chat Shown Go back to a checkpoint /review /context Chat Shown Show the conversation /robot Chat Shown ASCII robot art /robots Chat Shown Show the active robot(s) /ruby /rb Chat Sent Run Ruby (needs --allow-ruby-eval) /say Chat Shown Speak text aloud /skill Both Sent Insert a skill's text /skills Chat Shown List skills /spawn Chat Next prompt One-off specialist robot /task Chat Sent Create a TrakFlow task /tasks /tf Chat Sent Show TrakFlow ready tasks /temperature /temp Chat Shown Set temperature /tools Chat Shown List available tools /top_p /topp Chat Shown Set top-p /verify Chat Next prompt Two answers plus reconciliation /webpage /website, /web Both Sent Insert a web page as Markdown

Front matter keys such as next: and pipeline: aren't directives. See Prompt Files. There are no /next or /pipeline chat directives.

docs.title: /add_recruit
docs.text:
Aliases: /add · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/add_recruit NAME [PROVIDER/MODEL] [skill:ID[,ID...]] [SYSTEM PROMPT...]

Adds a robot named NAME to the crew. A recruit stays for the rest of the session, and you can address it with @NAME.

  • With only a name, the recruit uses the session's model.
  • Use - or inherit in place of a model to keep the session's model while still giving a system prompt.
  • Each skill:ID token assigns one or more skills. The skills become the recruit's role.
  • Everything after the model is the recruit's system prompt.
/add_recruit critic openai/gpt-4o You are a blunt code reviewer.
/add tester - skill:rspec_writer

AIA replies Recruited 'critic' into the crew (openai/gpt-4o). If it can't add the recruit, it replies Recruit failed: .... See Crews.

docs.title: /available_models
docs.text:
Aliases: /am, /available, /models, /all_models, /llms · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/available_models [TERM ...]

Lists models with their provider, input price per million tokens, context window, modalities and capabilities.

  • A plain term (or +term) keeps the models whose entry contains it.
  • -term, ~term or !term removes the models whose entry contains it.
  • A term with _to_, such as text_to_image, filters by modality.
  • If your current model has a provider/ prefix, AIA asks that provider for its live model list instead.
/models claude -haiku
/am text_to_image

docs.title: /checkpoint
docs.text:
Aliases: /ckp, /cp · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/checkpoint [NAME]

Saves the current conversation under NAME. Without a name, checkpoints are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on. Checkpoints last only for the current session.

/checkpoint before_refactor
Checkpoint 'before_refactor' created at position 6.

docs.title: /checkpoints_list
docs.text:
Aliases: /checkpoints · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

Lists the saved checkpoints with their position, the time each was created, and a preview of the last message you sent before it.

/checkpoints

=== Available Checkpoints ===
  before_refactor: position 6, created 14:02:11
    → "Now refactor the parser to use a state machine"
=== End of Checkpoints ===

docs.title: /clear
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/clear [--all]

Removes the conversation history from every robot in the session. The system prompt is kept unless you add --all. All checkpoints are deleted too.

/clear
Chat context cleared.

docs.title: /compare
docs.text:
Aliases: /cmp · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/compare PROMPT --models MODEL1,MODEL2[,...]

Sends the prompt to each listed model separately and prints each response under the model's name. The models don't see your conversation.

Every word that isn't part of --models belongs to the prompt.

/compare Write a haiku about autumn --models gpt-4o-mini,claude-haiku-4-5

docs.title: /concurrent
docs.text:
Aliases: /conc · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Next prompt

Runs your next message with your MCP servers split into independent groups that are queried in parallel. This needs more than one MCP server that is relevant to the prompt, in at least two groups. Otherwise the message runs normally. To do this automatically on every prompt, use --concurrent-auto. See MCP Servers.

/concurrent
Compare the open GitHub issues with the TODOs in the local repository.

docs.title: /config
docs.text:
Aliases: /cfg · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/config                  # show every setting
/config SECTION          # show one top-level section, e.g. llm, flags, output
/config KEY VALUE        # change a setting

KEY can be:

  • An option name, such as temperature, max_tokens, debug, verbose, consensus or tokens
  • A dotted path, such as llm.max_tokens or output.file

The change lasts for the rest of the session only. Model settings such as temperature, top_p and llm.* apply from your next message: AIA retunes the running robot, and every crewmate, without losing the conversation. See Configuration Precedence. AIA warns Unknown config option 'x' if it doesn't recognize the key.

/config llm
/config debug true
/config llm.max_tokens 4000

Value types

AIA converts the value to the setting's type: numbers for temperature or llm.max_tokens, true/false for on/off settings (true, yes, on, 1 / false, no, off, 0), and comma-separated lists for list settings. A value that doesn't fit is stored as you typed it.

docs.title: /cost
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

Prints a CSV table of the session's turns. It shows the model, input, output and total tokens, the cost and the elapsed time for each turn, followed by a TOTAL row. If an output file is set, the CSV is also appended to it.

/cost

model,input_tokens,output_tokens,total_tokens,cost,elapsed
gpt-4o-mini,412,256,668,$0.00022,2.1s
TOTAL,412,256,668,$0.00022,2.1s

docs.title: /debate
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Next prompt

Your next message becomes the subject of a debate among the robots in the session. The debate runs at least 2 rounds and at most 5, and stops early when the robots agree. You need at least two robots, from several models (--model a,b) or from recruits. With only one robot, the message runs normally. See Advanced Modes.

/debate
Should a small team start with a monolith or microservices?

docs.title: /decompose
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Next prompt

Splits your next message into independent sub-tasks, runs them in parallel, and combines the results. Timing figures show how long the work took in parallel compared with one after another. If the message can't usefully be split, it runs normally.

/decompose
Summarize the pros and cons of Postgres, MySQL and SQLite for a mobile backend.

docs.title: /delegate
docs.text:
Aliases: /del · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Next prompt

Breaks your next message into sub-tasks, assigns each one to a robot in the crew, records the plan in TrakFlow, and runs it. This needs more than one robot and an initialized TrakFlow project (tf init). Otherwise the message runs normally.

/delegate
Design the database schema, write the migration, and write tests for it.

docs.title: /drop_recruit
docs.text:
Aliases: /drop · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/drop_recruit NAME

Removes a recruit from the crew.

/drop critic
Dropped 'critic' from the crew.

docs.title: /help
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

Lists every directive, including custom ones, grouped by category with their aliases and descriptions.

docs.title: /include
docs.text:
Use in: Both · Chat output: Sent

/include PATH                       # chat
<%= include 'PATH' %>               # prompt file

Inserts another file after processing it as a prompt. Its shell references, ERB and parameters are all handled, and it can include other files in turn. In a prompt file, PATH is relative to the directory of the file that contains the tag. In chat, it is relative to your current directory. Include loops are detected and stop with an error. include isn't available in executable or piped prompts. Use insert there.

<%= include 'shared/house_style.md' %>

docs.title: /insert
docs.text:
Aliases: /read · Use in: Both · Chat output: Sent

/insert PATH
<%= insert 'PATH' %>

Inserts a file's text exactly as it is, with no shell expansion, ERB or parameters. Paths resolve the same way as for include, or against the current directory when there is no prompt file.

Review this code:

<%= insert 'lib/parser.rb' %>

docs.title: /mcp
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

Shows how many MCP servers are defined, connected and failed. It lists each connected server's tools and the error for each failed server.

/mcp

MCP Server Status
=================
Defined: 2  Connected: 1  Failed: 1

Connected Servers:
  github (26 tools)
    - list_issues
    ...
Failed Servers:
  postgres: connection refused

docs.title: /model
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/model                       # show details of the current model(s)
/model MODEL[,MODEL...]      # switch to one or more models

With no argument, AIA shows the current model's details. With several models, it shows each one's provider, context window, prices and capabilities.

Switching keeps your conversation: by default the old model summarizes it for the new one. Set model_switch_history to replay (re-send your messages) or clean (start fresh). MODEL can also be an alias such as sonnet or cheap, or one you define under model_aliases.

See Choosing Models.

/model claude-sonnet-4
/model gpt-4o,claude-sonnet-4

docs.title: /orchestrate
docs.text:
Aliases: /orch · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Next prompt

Treats your next message as a set of application requirements. Three tiers of robots work on it: an orchestrator, lead agents and specialists. See Advanced Modes.

/orchestrate
Build a command-line tool that tracks reading habits, with a SQLite store and a weekly report.

docs.title: /paste
docs.text:
Aliases: /clipboard · Use in: Both · Chat output: Sent

Inserts the text on your system clipboard.

/paste

Fix the grammar in this paragraph:

<%= paste %>

docs.title: /plan
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Sent

/plan DESCRIPTION

Creates a TrakFlow item from the description. This needs an initialized TrakFlow project (tf init). Otherwise AIA prints TrakFlow not available. Run 'tf init' to initialize a project.

/plan Migrate the reporting jobs from cron to Solid Queue

docs.title: /plugins
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

Lists the plugins that are currently loaded, by file name without .rb.

docs.title: /reskill
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/reskill NAME [skill:ID[,ID...]] [SYSTEM PROMPT...]

Clears a crew member's conversation and gives it new skills, a new system prompt, or both.

/reskill critic skill:security_review
Reskilled 'critic' with security_review (clean slate).

docs.title: /restore
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/restore [NAME]

Returns the conversation to a checkpoint. Everything after it is discarded, and so are any checkpoints saved after it. Without a name, AIA restores the checkpoint before the most recent one. That takes at least two checkpoints.

/restore before_refactor
Context restored to checkpoint 'before_refactor' (position 6).

docs.title: /review
docs.text:
Aliases: /context · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

Prints the conversation so far, one numbered line per message, with 📍 markers where checkpoints were saved. Long messages are shortened, and tool calls are summarized.

docs.title: /robot
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

Prints AIA's ASCII robot.

docs.title: /robots
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

Shows the active robot or robots and the mode: Single, Crew, Parallel, Pipeline or Consensus. For each robot it shows the model and provider, the cost per 1K input and output tokens, how many local and MCP tools it has, and its role.

docs.title: /ruby
docs.text:
Aliases: /rb · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Sent

/ruby RUBY CODE

Evaluates one line of Ruby and sends the result to the model. Disabled by default. Enable it with --allow-ruby-eval, or with flags: { allow_ruby_eval: true } in ~/.config/aia/aia.yml. While it is disabled, the directive only prints an error. While it is enabled, AIA prints a warning to STDERR before it runs the code. If the code raises an error, the error message is sent in place of a result.

/ruby Dir.glob('spec/**/*_spec.rb').size

See ERB & Shell and Security.

docs.title: /say
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/say TEXT

Speaks the text with your speak command (--speak-command or audio.speak_command; the macOS say command by default). With say, AIA uses your voice (--voice or audio.voice) if you've set one. Without text, AIA prints Usage: /say TEXT and sends nothing to the model. To have every response spoken, use --speak. See Images & Speech.

/say The build is green

docs.title: /skill
docs.text:
Use in: Both · Chat output: Sent

/skill ID
<%= skill 'ID' %>

Inserts the SKILL.md text of a skill from your skills directory (default ~/.prompts/skills). ID can be the start of a skill's directory name, or a path that begins with /, ./, ../ or ~/, to a skill folder or to a .md / .markdown file. See Roles & Skills.

/skill changelog

docs.title: /skills
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/skills [TERM ...]

Lists the skills in your skills directory with their name and description. Terms filter the list by the text of each skill's front matter: a plain term must appear, and a -term must not.

/skills ruby -rails

docs.title: /spawn
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Next prompt

/spawn                                       # AIA picks a specialist for the next prompt
/spawn TYPE                                  # a specialist of this kind
/spawn NAME PROVIDER/MODEL [SYSTEM PROMPT]   # exactly the specialist you describe

Creates a one-off specialist robot to answer your next message. Unlike a recruit, a spawned specialist doesn't join the crew. In the full form, use - or inherit as the model to keep the session's model, and add skill:<id> to give the specialist a skill. A specialist gets the chief's tools and MCP servers. See Crews.

/spawn security
Review this login controller for vulnerabilities: <%= insert 'app/controllers/sessions_controller.rb' %>

docs.title: /task
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Sent

/task TITLE

Creates a TrakFlow task with the given title. Like /plan, it needs an initialized TrakFlow project.

/task Add retry logic to the webhook sender

docs.title: /tasks
docs.text:
Aliases: /tf · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Sent

/tasks             # ready tasks
/tasks summary     # project summary

Shows TrakFlow tasks that are ready to work on, or a summary of the project.

docs.title: /temperature
docs.text:
Aliases: /temp · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/temperature VALUE

Sets the sampling temperature for the rest of the session. Lower values give more focused answers, and higher values give more varied ones. This is the same as /config temperature VALUE. In 2.0.0 the robot that is already running keeps its old temperature. The new value applies after you switch with /model, and to robots built later in the session.

/temp 0.2

docs.title: /tools
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/tools [FILTER]

Lists the tools the model can call, both local and MCP, with their descriptions. FILTER keeps only the tools whose name or description contains that text. See Tools.

/tools file

docs.title: /top_p
docs.text:
Aliases: /topp · Use in: Chat · Chat output: Shown

/top_p VALUE

Sets top-p (nucleus) sampling for the rest of the session. This is the same as /config top_p VALUE. Like /temperature, it doesn't change the robot that is already running until you switch with /model. Some providers reject requests that set both temperature and top-p.

docs.title: /verify
docs.text:
Use in: Chat · Chat output: Next prompt

Gets two independent answers to your next message, then reconciles them into one answer. This is useful for questions where a single answer might be confidently wrong.

/verify
How many weekdays are there between 2026-11-02 and 2026-12-25 inclusive?

docs.title: /webpage
docs.text:
Aliases: /website, /web · Use in: Both · Chat output: Sent

/webpage URL
<%= webpage 'URL' %>

Fetches a web page through the pure.md service and inserts it as Markdown. This requires the PUREMD_API_KEY environment variable. Without it, AIA prints ERROR: PUREMD_API_KEY is required in order to include a webpage.

/web https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master/NEWS_md.html

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Directives: concepts, categories and writing your own
  • Chat Sessions: directives in everyday chat
  • CLI Options: the command-line equivalents of many settings

docs.title: FAQ & Troubleshooting
docs.text: Answers to common questions, and fixes for the messages you are most likely to see. Error messages are quoted exactly as aia prints them, so you can search this page for yours.

docs.title: Which API key do I need?
docs.text:
The one for the provider of the model you use. The default model, gpt-4o-mini, needs OPENAI_API_KEY; Claude models need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; local models through Ollama or LM Studio need none. aia --list-providers marks the providers that have a key set:

$ aia --list-providers | grep 'has API key'
- anthropic (has API key)

See Environment Variables.

docs.title: How do I change the default model?
docs.text:
For one run, -m: aia -m claude-haiku-4-5 my_prompt. For every run, put it in ~/.config/aia/aia.yml:

models:
  - name: claude-haiku-4-5

or export AIA_MODEL=claude-haiku-4-5. See Choosing Models.

docs.title: How do I find a model's exact name?
docs.text:
aia --available-models sonnet               # search the model registry
aia --provider ollama --list-models         # what a provider is serving right now

docs.title: Why is there a temp.md in every directory I use aia in?
docs.text:
Responses are written to temp.md by default as well as to the screen. Pass --no-output or -o somewhere.md, or set it in your config file:

output:
  file: false

(file: ~ doesn't work: a null in the config file is ignored and the default remains.)

docs.title: How do I leave a chat session?
docs.text: Type exit, press Enter on an empty line, or press Ctrl+C. See Chat Sessions.

docs.title: Where are my prompts?
docs.text: In ~/.prompts, unless you've set --prompts-dir, prompts.dir or AIA_PROMPTS__DIR. aia doesn't create the directory or ship any prompts; you write your own. See Your First Prompt.

docs.title: A prompt ID is required unless you use --chat, --fuzzy, --pipeline or --role, …
docs.text: You ran aia with nothing to send. Context files on their own are not a prompt. Give a prompt ID (aia my_prompt), a pipeline (aia -p draft,polish), a role (aia -r editor), start a chat (aia --chat), pick a prompt with aia --fuzzy, or pipe in some text.

docs.title: No prompt named 'my_prompt' in … (and no file by that name).
docs.text:
aia looked for ~/.prompts/my_prompt.md and for a file called my_prompt, and found neither. If a prompt has a similar name, the message ends with Did you mean: …?. Usually it is:

  • a typo in the prompt ID;
  • a prompt in a different directory — check ls ~/.prompts/my_prompt.md, or add --prompts-dir;
  • a prompt in a subdirectory — include the subdirectory: aia dev/my_prompt;
  • a file with an extension other than .md.

docs.title: Error: Prompt ID 'draftt' does not exist at /Users/you/.prompts/draftt.md
docs.text: One of the prompts in a pipeline (-p, -n, or next:/pipeline: in front matter) doesn't exist. aia checks them all before running anything and ends with One or more prompt IDs do not exist.

docs.title: Unknown argument(s): _B / Did you mean: -B?
docs.text: An option was typed with an underscore instead of a dash. Use -B.

docs.title: ERROR: invalid option: --terse
docs.text: The option doesn't exist. --terse, --regex and --skills-prefix were removed in 2.0; see Upgrading to 2.0. Otherwise check spelling against aia --help.

docs.title: ERROR: invalid argument: -t hot
docs.text: An option got a value of the wrong kind: -t, --top-p and the penalties need a number, --max-tokens and --refresh a whole number, and --tool-approval one of ask, approve, deny. The message names the option and the value it rejected.

docs.title: Role file not found: …/roles/reviewer.md
docs.text: You used -m MODEL=ROLE and the role file doesn't exist. The message lists the roles that do exist. aia --list-roles shows what is available. See Roles & Skills.

docs.title: Warning: Invalid role ID or file not found: roles/reviewer
docs.text: The role given with -r isn't in your roles directory. Run aia --list-roles, or give a path to the role file: -r ./reviewer.md.

docs.title: ERROR: Config file not found: …
docs.text: The file given to -c doesn't exist. Check the path; ~ is expanded for you.

docs.title: ERROR: Invalid log level 'loud'. Must be one of: debug, info, warn, error, fatal
docs.text: Use one of the five listed levels with --log-level.

docs.title: Error: 'fzf' is not installed. Please install 'fzf' to use the --fuzzy option.
docs.text: Install fzf (brew install fzf, apt install fzf …) or name the prompt instead.

docs.title: ERROR: --list-models requires --provider SLUG …
docs.text: --list-models asks one provider what it serves. Add --provider, for example aia --provider ollama --list-models, or search all known models with --available-models.

docs.title: ERROR: unknown provider 'olama'. Registered providers: …
docs.text: The --provider slug isn't one aia knows. Pick one from the list printed with the error. A provider that comes from a separate gem appears once the gem is installed (or loaded with --require).

docs.title: file/dir path is not valid: … or file should have *.rb extension: …
docs.text: --tools was given a path that doesn't exist, or a file that isn't .rb. Directories are fine; aia loads every .rb file in them.

docs.title: NoMethodError mentioning param when loading a tool
docs.text: The tool is written for aia 1.x. Change param :x, desc: "…" to parameter :x, description: "…". See Upgrading to 2.0.

docs.title: ERROR: /ruby is disabled. …
docs.text: /ruby is off by default. Start aia with --allow-ruby-eval, or set flags.allow_ruby_eval: true in ~/.config/aia/aia.yml. Read Security first.

docs.title: ERROR: PUREMD_API_KEY is required in order to include a webpage
docs.text: /webpage fetches pages through the pure.md service, which needs an API key in PUREMD_API_KEY.

docs.title: Warning: Skill 'x' not found in … / Warning: SKILL.md not found in …
docs.text: A skill named with -s or /skill isn't a subdirectory of your skills directory, or the subdirectory has no SKILL.md. Run aia --list-skills. Remember that the skills directory is ~/.prompts/skills unless you set skills.dir / --skills-dir; it doesn't follow --prompts-dir.

docs.title: Warning: configured plugins directory does not exist: …
docs.text: --plugins-dir, paths.plugins_dir or AIA_PLUGINS_DIR points at a missing directory. Create it or fix the setting.

docs.title: ERROR: The shell 'tcsh' is not supported or the completion script is missing.
docs.text: --completion supports bash, zsh and fish.

docs.title: An MCP server shows as failed at startup
docs.text:
Failed servers are named in the startup banner, and /mcp in chat shows each one's error. Common causes:

  • The command isn't installed or not on your PATH. Run the server's command and args yourself in a terminal.
  • Two servers offer a tool with the same name. The second one fails. Add prefix: to one of them.
  • The server uses the sse or ws transport, which aia 2.0 no longer supports. Use its Streamable HTTP url: or run it over stdio.
  • It took too long. All servers together get concurrency.mcp_timeout seconds (120 by default) to connect; stragglers fail with global connection timeout (120s).

aia --mcp-list shows what is configured; aia --mcp-list --list-tools connects to each server and lists its tools. See MCP Servers.

docs.title: WARNING: --mcp-use specified server(s) not found in config: …
docs.text: A name given to --mcp-use doesn't match any configured server. The next line lists the available names.

docs.title: Warning: MCP config file not found: … / Warning: Invalid JSON in MCP config file …
docs.text: The file given to --mcp is missing or isn't valid JSON. aia skips it and carries on.

docs.title: The model never uses my tool
docs.text:
• Run aia --list-tools with the same --tools / --require options to confirm the tool loads.
  • Check --allowed-tools and --rejected-tools (or tools.allowed / tools.rejected): they match by substring, so --rt read also removes spreadsheet_reader.
  • The automatic tool filter offers only tools that look relevant to your prompt. Try --no-auto-tool-filter, or use -v to see which tools were offered on each turn.
  • Not every model supports tool calling.

docs.title: Tool calls are refused when I run aia from a script
docs.text: Tools from MCP servers marked requires_approval: ask before running. With no terminal to ask on, the default ask mode refuses. For unattended runs, decide explicitly with --tool-approval approve or --tool-approval deny. See Security.

docs.title: My setting isn't taking effect
docs.text:
Work through Troubleshooting a setting. The usual suspects:

  • An exported AIA_* variable overriding your config file (env | grep '^AIA_').
  • A config/aia.yml in the current directory.
  • A YAML mistake in ~/.config/aia/aia.yml: if the file can't be parsed aia ignores the whole file.
  • A -c file, which replaces your personal config entirely.
  • A key that has no effect in 2.0.0 — these are marked in Configuration Keys.

aia --dump /tmp/c.yml shows the configuration aia ends up with.

docs.title: An AIA_* variable doesn't seem to work
docs.text: aia converts each value to the setting's type (on/off words, numbers, comma-separated lists). A value that doesn't fit, such as AIA_LLM__MAX_TOKENS=lots, is kept as text and may not work. aia --dump /tmp/c.yml shows what aia made of it. See Environment Variables.

docs.title: Can I have per-project settings?
docs.text: Yes. Put a config/aia.yml in the project and run aia from the project's root; it is layered over your personal config. Or keep complete setups in separate files and pick one with -c.

docs.title: Shell completion doesn't offer my prompts
docs.text: The completion scripts list .md files under $AIA_PROMPTS__DIR, or ~/.prompts when it is unset. They can't read your config file, so if your prompts live somewhere else, export AIA_PROMPTS__DIR in your shell — setting prompts.dir in the config file isn't enough. See --completion.

docs.title: I see <think> sections — or I want to see them
docs.text: Some local models write their reasoning inside <think> tags. aia hides it by default; --thinking shows it.

docs.title: How do I see what a run costs?
docs.text: --tokens shows tokens and elapsed time after each turn, --cost adds the price. In chat, /cost prints the session so far as CSV.

docs.title: Switching models with /model kept the old conversation
docs.text: That's deliberate: the new model is given a summary of the conversation. Use /clear after switching if you want a fresh start.

docs.title: How do I get debugging information?
docs.text:
aia --debug --log-to /tmp/aia.log my_prompt

--debug sets all logs to debug level; --log-to collects them in one file. Use --log-level info for less detail.

docs.title: migrate_prompts runs but prints nothing
docs.text: It reports through Ruby's warning channel, which RUBYOPT=-W0 silences. Run RUBYOPT= ruby bin/migrate_prompts --dry-run. See Migrating Prompts.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
• aia --help lists every option; /help in chat lists every directive.
  • Report an issue on GitHub, including aia --version, the command you ran and the full message.
